fx_note: FCT.NZ is a thin secondary NZX listing (NZD-quoted) of a UK primary-listed, GBP-reporting closed-end investment trust (LSE: FCIT). All fundamental data (NAV, dividends, discount history, ongoing charges, gearing) is GBP/pence. current_price and all intrinsic_value/entry_price fields are reported in NZD (to match the NZX quote the user tracks) by converting the GBP-derived valuation at the live GBPNZD rate. A parallel 'gbp' sub-object under each block gives the native pence figures for direct comparison against FCIT.L. Cross-check at valuation date: FCIT.L 342.4p x GBPNZD 2.2898 = NZD 7.84 vs the actual NZX quote of NZD 7.81, a 0.4% gap - the arbitrage is tight and the NZX quote is judged fair/liquid enough to use directly rather than a synthetic cross-rate price. NZ holders receive NO imputation/franking credits on UK-sourced dividends and bear fully unhedged GBP/NZD translation risk stacked on top of the trust's own multi-currency (USD ~60%, EUR, JPY) portfolio exposure; NZ FIF/FDR tax rules likely apply for most retail holders, a further drag on the practical return not modelled here.
share_split_note: 4-for-1 share sub-division effective 11 May 2026 (each 25p ordinary became four 6.25p ordinaries). ALL per-share figures in this model (NAV, EPS, DPS) are POST-SPLIT. The Metrics CSV is already restated post-split throughout its full history (e.g. FY2025 EPS 0.3464 = 34.64p, DPS 0.0415 = 4.15p); no further adjustment has been applied here.
valuation_philosophy: F&C Investment Trust (founded 1868, the world's oldest collective investment scheme) is a GBP6.86bn UK closed-end investment trust holding a globally diversified portfolio of ~400 listed equities plus a ~11% private equity sleeve, benchmarked to the FTSE All-World Index and managed externally by Columbia Threadneedle. It is NOT an operating business: there is no revenue, EBITDA, capex, working-capital cycle, or free cash flow in the standard sense. 'OperatingCashFlow' in the Metrics CSV is dividends received less management costs and finance costs - it is portfolio income, not FCF, and is not used here. 'NetIncome' is the statutory total return (revenue account + capital account), which is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio revaluation and swings enormously half-on-half (H1-2022 -GBP630.1m total return vs FY2021 +GBP919.3m) - it is never CAGR'd or projected directly. A standard FCF/WACC/Gordon-growth DCF is therefore INAPPLICABLE and has not been built. Instead this model uses the NAV-compounding + exit-discount framework already applied consistently to the other closed-end funds/investment trusts in this research folder (BIT.NZ, AFI.NZ, FIH.U, FRFHF): (1) build a NAV-per-share total-return assumption from components (long-run global-equity gross return, less the 0.45% ongoing-charges drag which is treated as already embedded in the historical realised NAV-TR figures used to calibrate the assumption, plus a small buyback-accretion credit); (2) project NAV per share and the progressive dividend forward 5 years; (3) apply a scenario exit discount/premium to the year-5 NAV, since the market-clearing valuation metric for a trust is its price/NAV discount, not an earnings multiple; (4) headline intrinsic value = TODAY's (30-Jun-2026) NAV per share x (1 - scenario fair discount) - i.e. what a rational buyer should pay for today's known NAV at a fair (rather than the current live 8.7%) discount; (5) a separate 5-year IRR-build (PV of interim dividends + PV of year-5 exit value at cost of equity) is shown as a cross-check/memo capturing NAV compounding over the horizon, and is the basis for the entry-price calculation. NO DOUBLE-COUNTING OF DEBT: NAV per share is ALREADY stated net of all borrowings (the trust's GBP544m of long-term loans plus short-term RCF drawdowns are deducted inside the published NAV figure) - portfolio gearing (4.5% at fair value / 5.7% including derivatives at 30-Jun-2026) is captured entirely inside the NAV-total-return assumption as a return amplifier, and net debt has NOT been separately subtracted anywhere in this model. Subtracting a net-debt figure from NAV a second time would be the single easiest way to badly misvalue this ticker, and has been deliberately avoided. THE CENTRAL VALUATION FINDING: F&C's cost of equity (~9%, appropriate for a large, liquid, globally diversified FTSE-100 equity fund - NOT the 17-20% small-cap/illiquidity premiums used elsewhere in this repo) is very close to its own realistic expected NAV total return (~7.5% base case, after the ~1.1% dividend payout is netted out of a ~7.5% gross total-return assumption). Because expected return and the discount rate are nearly equal, the trust is close to fairly valued at its current ~8.7% discount to NAV, and essentially all of the available edge is in the discount narrowing or widening from here - there is very little edge in the NAV-compounding engine itself, which is priced efficiently. This produces a small, honest base-case result rather than a manufactured large upside or downside.

inputs.nav_asof: 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 half-year report, released 2026-08-03), post 4-for-1 split, debt at fair value basis
inputs.nav_debt_basis_note: Uses the debt-at-fair-value NAV basis (375.18p), which is the Company's own headline KPI and the basis on which its published discount is calculated.
inputs.gearing_note: Portfolio gearing amplifies both directions and is captured inside the total_return_pct assumption, not modelled as a separate net-debt subtraction - NAV per share is already net of all borrowings.
inputs.dividend_track_record: 55 consecutive years of dividend increases (158th consecutive annual payment) as of FY2025 (+6.4% to 4.15p post-split), 56th rise flagged for FY2026 (first interim 0.99p declared); fully covered by earnings of 4.49p; revenue reserve GBP125.5m at FY2025 (GBP136.6m at H1-2026) provides additional cover.
inputs.units: millions except per-share figures (pence) and NAV/price data
inputs.sbc_note: Not applicable - F&C is an externally-managed investment trust (Columbia Threadneedle); no employees, no stock-based compensation, no dilution mechanic, no capex, no working-capital cycle exists in this model.
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable - see valuation_philosophy. No FCF projection, WACC-Gordon terminal value, or SBC adjustment is used; those schema fields below are populated with null plus explanatory notes for schema consistency with operating-company DCFs, and are replaced functionally by the NAV-compounding equivalents.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable - not applicable to an externally-managed investment trust; see fcf_dcf_note
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Real cash outflow in financing activities (not an announced authorization). Buybacks reduce share count and are NAV-per-share accretive when executed at a discount to NAV - modelled as a small (~0.12%/yr) direct addition to the NAV growth rate (buyback_pct ~1.5%/yr x current ~8% discount), not as a share-count projection mechanic.
inputs.projected_shares_note: Held flat for projection purposes. Continued buybacks are modelled as NAV-accretive (embedded in the total-return assumption) rather than as a separate share-count mechanic, since (unlike an SBC-diluting operating company) there is no offsetting dilution to net against.
inputs.currency_note: Fundamentals (NAV, income, net assets) are GBP; valuation outputs (intrinsic_value, entry_price) are reported in NZD to match the FCT.NZ quote, converted at GBPNZD 2.2898. Native pence figures are in the "gbp" sub-object.

historical_growth.methodology: F&C's own preferred value driver is NAV-per-share TOTAL RETURN (NAV growth + dividends paid), disclosed against the FTSE All-World Index benchmark. Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs are shown below for schema completeness but are NOT the growth driver used in projections - NetIncome/EPS for a trust is dominated by unrealised/realised capital gains timing (H1-2022 total return -GBP630.1m vs FY2021 +GBP919.3m) rather than an operating trend, and 'Revenue' is investment/dividend income only.
historical_growth.nav_per_share_capital_only_cagr_methodol: Derived directly from the Metrics CSV as ShareholdersEquity / SharesOutstanding for each period (FY2017 169.13p, FY2020 210.17p, FY2025 325.16p, H1-2026 364.15p, all post-split). This is a CAPITAL-ONLY NAV CAGR (excludes the ~1.1-2% dividend yield paid out along the way) and cross-checks closely against the reported +10.0% p.a. 20-year NAV total-return figure once the dividend yield is added back.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nav_total_return_base_case_assumption (not a pure historical CAGR - see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR is not meaningful for this ticker (NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings on the same order of magnitude as the share count, e.g. H1-2022 EPS -0.300 vs H1-2021 EPS 0.241) and is left null rather than computed. Equity (net assets) CAGR (6.6-6.9%) sits BELOW the NAV-per-share CAGR (8.5-9.1%) because the sustained buyback programme has shrunk the share count materially (2,168.7m at FY2017 vs 1,884.9m at H1-2026, a ~13% reduction) while still growing total net assets - net assets grew slower than NAV-per-share by design, the opposite direction of a dilutive operating company.
historical_growth.notes: F&C's own realised NAV total return has RECENTLY LAGGED its FTSE All-World benchmark: -2.6pp in FY2025 (+11.6% vs +14.2%) and -0.2pp in H1-2026 (+12.4% vs +12.6%), reversing a period of outperformance in FY2024 (+1.7pp). The private equity sleeve (~11% of assets) has been a drag in both FY2024 and FY2025. The base-case 7.5% total-return assumption is built as a long-run global-equity nominal total-return expectation (~8.5-9% gross) net of a modest, partially-persisting benchmark-relative drag from the multi-sleeve/PE structure, and is meaningfully below both the exceptional FY2024 NAV TR of +21.0% and the benchmark's own longer-run averages - neither should be extrapolated. This is a deliberately conservative but not punitive assumption, consistent with a fund whose 20-year NAV TR has averaged 10.0% p.a. gross of the recent underperformance episode.

base.rationale: Long-run global equity total return (~8.5-9% gross) net of F&C's recently demonstrated benchmark-relative drag (FY2025 -2.6pp, H1-2026 -0.2pp; PE sleeve underperforming) only partially assumed to close, giving ~7.5% total return before the buyback-accretion credit. Exit discount holds roughly at the 2025 full-year average (7.9%) and near the 10-year historical average, reflecting the view that today's 8.7% live discount is close to the trust's own normal range rather than either a permanently closed or a structurally widening gap. Dividend growth assumed at the 10-year historical average (5.6%) rounded to 5.5%.

bull.rationale: Market leadership broadens beyond mega-cap tech (already visible in H1-2026), favouring F&C's diversified, less concentrated approach; the private equity sleeve closes its performance gap as underlying holdings (Schiehallion/Syncona names) mature or re-rate; the FCA's more favourable CCI cost-disclosure regime (mandatory from Jun-2027) plus continued buybacks and Saba-driven sector consolidation pressure narrow the discount toward the FY2019 near-par reading (the only time in 10 years F&C traded near/above NAV).

bear.rationale: Persistent benchmark underperformance continues as narrow AI/mega-cap-tech leadership persists and the AI-capex cycle moderates (management's own flagged risk), a global equity de-rating from current all-time highs hits a ~5-8% geared portfolio harder than the unlevered benchmark, the private equity sleeve remains a structural drag, and the sector-wide UK investment-trust de-rating (wealth-platform outflows, Saba activism notwithstanding) resumes, pushing the discount back out beyond the 2025 intra-year wide of 13.8% toward the FY2024 year-end level of 9.2% and further.

five_year_irr_build_memo.description: Cross-check to the headline 'current NAV x fair discount' intrinsic value: PV of the 5-year dividend stream plus PV of the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x scenario exit discount), both discounted at the scenario's cost of equity. This captures compounding of NAV growth over the horizon that the simpler current-NAV framing does not; it is also the basis for the entry-price calculation below (using base-case cashflows at the 15% hurdle instead of CoE).

base.terminal_pct_of_value: n/a - not an FCF DCF; see five_year_irr_build_memo (exit value is ~94% of the 5yr-build fair value)
base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - trust valuation uses P/NAV, not an earnings multiple

entry_price.methodology: Price today such that 5 years of projected base-case dividends plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x base-case -7.5% exit discount) discounted at 15% equals that price. Uses base-case cashflows only (per repo methodology).
entry_price.memo: A 15% IRR hurdle applied to a fund whose base-case expected total return is only ~7.5% p.a. mechanically requires buying at a very deep discount to today's NAV (~-32.6% vs today's 375.18p NAV, i.e. an entry P/NAV of ~0.67x) - DEEPER than F&C has ever traded in the available 10-year history (range 0.858x-1.015x, i.e. -14.2% to +1.5%). This is NOT an achievable near-term entry target; it should be read as 'this ticker cannot organically deliver a 15% forward IRR at any price it has historically reached', consistent with the equivalent finding for BIT.NZ. A globally diversified, low-cost, modestly geared equity trust with a ~7.5-9% expected total return should instead be judged against its cost of equity (~9%), not a 15%, private-equity-style hurdle. On that basis, buying today at NZD 7.81 (GBp 342.4, an 8.7% discount to the last published NAV) offers a prospective 5-year total return roughly in line with the base-case ~7.5% NAV total return, plus a small tailwind if the discount narrows toward its 7.5% base-case assumption from today's slightly wider 8.7% live reading - the headline base-case upside of +1.4-1.7% captures almost exactly that small discount-normalisation effect, nothing more.

sanity_check.description: For an investment trust the natural sanity anchor is price/NAV (P/NAV), not P/E or EV/EBITDA - both are set to null/n-a below because reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (H1-2022 total return -GBP630.1m, FY2021 +GBP919.3m) and there is no EBITDA concept for a portfolio of listed securities. The check trips if an implied scenario P/NAV falls outside the trust's own 10-year historical range of 0.858x (14.2% discount, FY2024 wide) to 1.015x (1.5% premium, FY2019) - none of the three scenarios below breach that range, so the check passes.

implied_multiples.price_to_earnings: n/a - NetIncome is mark-to-market, not an operating earnings concept
implied_multiples.ev_to_ebitda: n/a - no EBITDA concept for a listed-securities portfolio

sanity_check.diagnosis: All three DCF scenarios (P/NAV 0.87x-0.97x) sit comfortably inside F&C's own 10-year disclosed P/NAV range of 0.858x-1.015x, so the check passes by construction. The genuinely notable finding is that the LIVE market price today (342.4p vs 375.18p NAV = 8.74% discount, 0.9126x P/NAV) is WIDER than both the company's own reported 6.6% H1-2026 discount (based on a Board estimate that may use a slightly different intraday NAV snapshot) and the base-case assumption (7.5%) - i.e. the live discount has already drifted out modestly since the H1-2026 report date, which is the entire source of the small positive base-case upside reported above. P/E and EV/EBITDA are inapplicable for the reasons in 'description' and are reported as n/a rather than a fabricated figure.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required - no scenario breaches the historical range.

sensitivity.methodology: 5-year IRR-build fair value (PV of dividends + PV of exit value at year-5 NAV x row exit discount, both discounted at the 9.0% base-case cost of equity) in GBP pence, converted to NZD at 2.2898. Total return varied +/-2pp around the 7.5% base case; exit discount varied +/-4pp around the 7.5% base case.

probability_weighted.weighted_iv_currency_note: weighted_iv is stated in NZD to match the FCT.NZ quote currency used by the screener; weighted_iv_gbp_pence is the native London (FCIT.L) figure in pence.

discount_history_pct.note: Values as disclosed by the Company (positive = discount, negative = premium), on the debt-at-fair-value NAV basis. 2025 intra-year range was 3.6%-13.8% (avg 7.9%). FY2019 is the only year in the last decade F&C traded at a premium to NAV. Current live discount (8.7%, computed from the 342.4p FCIT.L price vs the 375.18p 30-Jun-2026 NAV) is modestly wider than both the Company's own reported H1-2026 point-in-time discount (6.6%) and the 2025 full-year average (7.9%), reflecting NAV drift since the last published figure.
